Read-only investigation in the treams-rs repository (integration checkout treams-rs, Python venv .venv, upstream treams source at scratch: treams and importable as treams in that venv if installed; check). Do NOT edit, commit or push anything in treams-rs, scratch: lanes/* or r4-tooling. Write any scratch scripts under cylbug/ and delete large outputs when done. Keep CPU use modest: run with taskset -c 3 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, because other jobs use CPUs 0-2.

Claim to verify (reported by another session; verify, do not assume it is right): PeriodicResponse.to_cylindrical (implemented via CylindricalTMatrix._from_response) gives wrong results when the CylindricalBasis has more than one axis (several positions), e.g. CylindricalBasis.diffr_orders(kz, mmax, lattice, bmax, 2, positions) as in treams' chain_tmatrixc example. Suspected cause: both conversions use every pair of positions, so cross-axis blocks are counted — expandlattice (cyl <- sph) on the outgoing side and diff.expansion / _native.cw_to_sw (sph <- cyl) on the incident side. treams masks both with to_basis.pidx[:, None] == basis.pidx (treams/_operators.py _sw_cw_expand, _cw_sw_expand). Reported effect: treams' chain_tmatrixc geometry (spheres at (-30,0,-75) and (30,0,75), radii 75/65, lattice 300, kz 0.005, k0 2*pi/700): E_z from the treams-rs cylindrical T-matrix is -2.102-0.150i against the exact -0.5263-0.0367i, while treams' two-axis result matches the exact value to 1e-8; the one-axis conversion is correct.

Tasks:

  1. Reproduce: a minimal script computing the same quantity with treams and with treams_rs, for one axis and for two axes. Report the numbers.
  2. Confirm or refute the cause by reading the treams-rs code path (python/treams_rs/... and the Rust it calls) and comparing with treams' _operators.py. Name exact files and line numbers.
  3. Describe the smallest correct fix (which functions, what mask, Python or Rust side), and whether single-axis (one position) results would stay bitwise identical after it (i.e. the fix only touches the multi-position case). Check whether other public functions share the same missing mask (e.g. other sw<->cw expansions, expand/expandlattice operators with multi-position cylindrical bases, translate helpers) — list each with a one-line verdict.
  4. Check whether the repository's deterministic dump scripts (gates/current/{uf_dump.py,hot_dump.py,lat_dump.py,battery.py}) exercise any multi-position cylindrical conversion; if they do, a fix would change recorded values. Return a concise report: verdict (bug confirmed or not), numbers, cause with file:line, proposed fix with an estimate of lines changed, the list of affected functions, and whether the fix keeps all existing recorded dumps identical.

Verdict: the bug is real, and the suspected cause is right

PeriodicResponse.to_cylindrical gives wrong results when the CylindricalBasis has more than one axis. CylindricalTMatrix._from_array is wrong too, because it uses the same _from_response. Cases with one axis are correct. I edited nothing in treams-rs (HEAD d95280b (condensed into 8251007)), the lanes or r4-tooling. The scratch scripts are in cylbug/ (repro.py, fixsim.py, sides.py, regular.py, battery_check.py, findpt.py), 32 KB in total. Everything ran with taskset -c 3 and one thread. The venv imports treams_rs from python and treams from site-packages.

1. Numbers (repro.py, fixsim.py)

The setup is treams' chain_tmatrixc geometry: k0 = 2π/700, eps = -16.5+1i, lmax = mmax = 3, period 300, kz = 0.005, bmax = 3.1·2π/300. E_z is the total field. The exact value is treams' spherical lattice sum, computed the way the example does with expandlattice onto a one-point spherical basis.

Case Point Exact treams treams_rs now
1 axis, 1 sphere (200,0,50) -0.459891+0.842844i -0.459892+0.842843i -0.459892+0.842843i
2 axes (200,0,50) -0.656334+0.563382i -0.656332+0.563375i -2.211460-0.199323i
2 axes (-250,40,-20) -0.564607-0.985938i -0.564607-0.985938i -1.305885-1.644127i
2 axes (0,150,120) 0.193684+0.245501i 0.193706+0.245521i -1.279060-0.384560i
  • One axis: the treams_rs and treams T-matrices differ by at most 2.8e-13 (largest entry 321).
  • Two axes: the T-matrices differ by up to 9.7e4 (largest treams entry 319). Every block is wrong, including the diagonal ones.
  • The claimed point: I could not find the point behind the reported -2.102-0.150i / -0.5263-0.0367i. The closest point on the example grid is (240,0,0), where treams gives -0.6504+0.5719i and treams_rs gives -2.0689-0.1435i. Over the grid's valid points, |treams_rs − treams| is 6.8 at most and 1.5 in the median.
  • Both sides matter: masking only the outgoing side, or only the incident side, still leaves an error of about 0.58. Both masks together match treams' TMatrixC.from_array to 1.9e-12.

2. Cause

  • Call path: python/treams_rs/_periodic.py:136-140 (to_cylindrical) calls python/treams_rs/_tmatrix.py:752-783 (_from_response).
    • Outgoing side (_tmatrix.py:766): expandlattice (_operators.py:508-529) → diff.periodic_to_cw (diff.py:1242) → crates/treams-py/src/basis.rs:415 → crates/treams-core/src/sw/periodic_to_cw.rs:100-141. Lines 124-125 there translate every sphere to every axis.
    • Incident side (_tmatrix.py:774): diff.expansion (diff.py:955, _native.cw_to_sw) → basis.rs:234 → crates/treams-core/src/cw/to_sw.rs:145-187. Line 79 translates every axis to every sphere.
  • This is documented behaviour: the _operators.py:167 and :474-475 docstrings say all origin pairs are included, "rather than an implicit matching-particle-index mask".
  • What treams does: it masks both conversions by to_basis.pidx[:, None] == basis.pidx, in _sw_cw_expand and _cw_sw_expand (venv treams/_operators.py:530 and :827; source scratch: treams/src/treams/_operators.py:600 and :897). TMatrixC.from_array is at scratch: treams/src/treams/_tmatrix.py:627-633.
  • Why all pairs is wrong here: with several axes, each axis block holds the whole field. Summing over all pairs counts every sphere's radiation once per axis, and every sphere's incident field once per axis. With a single axis there is nothing to double-count, and the all-pairs version is correct, including for several spheres off the axis.

3. Proposed fix (Python only, about 12–15 lines plus a test)

Add a helper, roughly:

def _axis_mask(cyl, sph):
    if len(cyl.positions) == 1:
        return None
    if len(cyl.positions) != len(sph.positions):
        raise ValueError("a multi-axis cylindrical basis needs one axis per particle position")
    return cyl.pidx[:, None] == sph.pidx
  • In _from_response, after line 776 and before response() runs, so the "validated before the solve" contract holds: if the mask is not None, set outgoing *= mask and incident *= mask.T.
  • In PeriodicWave.in_basis (_periodic.py:55-63), when the destination is cylindrical: conversion *= mask.
  • Add a regression test against treams.TMatrixC.from_array on the two-axis chain.

Keep the mask conditional on more than one axis. Applying it always would break the case that works today (one axis, several spheres): it drops the spheres whose index is not 0, and in my test the error went from 3e-3 to 0.42.

The fixed version also stays correct when the axes are not at the spheres' positions, because the Rust translation remains. Moving both axes to z=0 still matches the exact value at the truncation level (7e-6).

Single-axis results stay bitwise identical, because the new code never runs for one axis. I checked this with a monkeypatched version against all 128 battery cases, current vs fixed: 0 differences. Those cases include chain_to_cylindrical and chain_wave_cylindrical.

Do not mask in the Rust kernels or in diff.*. They are pairwise kernels with explicit origins, and the gradient tests (e.g. tests/lattice/test_periodic_conversion.py::test_periodic_conversion_all_pullbacks) and dump entries rely on all pairs.

Same missing mask in other functions

Function Verdict
PeriodicWave.in_basis(cyl with >1 axis, kind="outgoing") (_periodic.py:44-70) Bug, same cause. E_z -1.176+0.309i vs exact -0.656+0.563i; the mask fixes it.
CylindricalTMatrix._from_array (_tmatrix.py:729) Bug, shares _from_response.
operators.expand((sph, cyl)) regular, plus Wave.in_basis/expand and TMatrix.scatter(Wave) that call it Diverges from treams. Two axes count the incident field twice (norm ratio 1.998); the mask gives an exact match (5e-16). This is documented all-pairs behaviour, so changing it is an API decision.
operators.expandlattice((cyl, sph)) Diverges from treams, also documented. It is the root of the two bugs above.
_framework.Wave.in_basis (advect/jax/torch) Same behaviour as expand; no high-level to_cylindrical exists in those namespaces.
operators.translate OK, already masks (_operators.py:310).
Same-family expand and expandlattice (sph↔sph, cyl↔cyl) All pairs, the same as treams (no mask there either). OK.
plane wave → multipole, multipole → plane ports, SMatrix._from_response No destination origins, so not applicable. OK.
diff.expansion, diff.periodic_to_cw, advect.periodic_to_cw, _native.* Kernels; all pairs is their contract. Leave as is.
sw.periodic_to_cw, cw.to_sw Mode-label-only, no positions. Not applicable.

4. Recorded dumps

  • No dump runs to_cylindrical, _from_array or PeriodicWave.in_basis with more than one axis. The battery solve_periodic_* cases use one sphere on one axis. lat_dump.py and hot_dump.py (field evaluation only, no conversion) contain no cylindrical conversion. uf_dump.py re-runs the battery cases, which are covered by the 128-case check.
  • The proposed fix keeps every recorded dump identical.
  • Multi-position cross-family conversions do appear in the dumps, but only through the public operators and the kernels:
    • battery operators_expand.*.cw_sw (battery.py:1325, both bases have 2 positions) would change only if the public expand were masked.
    • battery operators_expandlattice.*.sw2cw (2216-2217, one axis, 2 spheres) would change, and become wrong, only with an unconditional mask.
    • battery diff_expansion_cylindrical cw2sw.* (1299-1302), battery diff_periodic_conversion, and uf_dump expansion.cyl2sph.* and periodic_conversion.* (415-433) would change only if the kernels were changed.
